string-array.name: grounding_prompts
string-array.item: Look around and find three green things
Feel the weight of your feet on the ground
Put the phone down, pour a glass of water and drink it slowly
Listen: what is the farthest sound you can hear?
Let your shoulders relax and sink a little
Look out the window at the farthest point and rest your eyes
Touch something nearby and notice its warmth and texture
Stand up and stretch, letting your back slowly lengthen
Think of one small thing that went well today
Take a deep breath and notice what the air smells like
Find the brightest color in front of you and rest your eyes on it
Talk to someone nearby, or look up at the sky
Count how many different sounds you can hear right now
Rub your palms warm and rest them gently over your eyes
Slowly roll your neck, once to the left, once to the right
Look outside: what color is the sky right now?
Unclench your jaw and let your teeth part a little
Wiggle your toes and feel them inside your shoes or socks
Step to a window or door and feel the air outside
Find something you haven\'t noticed in a while and really look at it

Rest a hand on your chest and feel it rise and fall
Take a sip of water and feel it go all the way down
Walk slowly to another room and back
Make a tight fist for a count of five, then slowly let go

Sit up a little and let the top of your head reach gently upward
Run a hand along your arm and feel the fabric of your sleeve
Look at the nearest plant, or picture a tree you like
Of everything you just scrolled past, what do you still remember? Let the rest go
Put one thing on the table back where it belongs
Close your eyes and count five breaths

string-array.name: grounding_prompts_bedtime
string-array.item: Charge your phone somewhere out of reach
Dim the lights in your room a little
Tomorrow\'s things can wait until tomorrow
Breathe out slowly and let your shoulders relax
Take a small sip of warm water and get ready for bed
Think of one small thing you\'re grateful for today
Pull up the covers and let yourself get warm
Close your eyes and listen to the quiet of the room
Write one thing for tomorrow on paper, then let it go
Brush your teeth and wash your face so your body knows it\'s time to sleep
Starting from your toes, let each part of your body relax in turn
Change into something comfortable to sleep in
Once the alarm is set, there\'s no need to check the phone again
Draw the curtains and let the room go dark
You did enough today. The rest can wait for tomorrow
Read a few pages of a paper book until you feel sleepy
Let your breathing slow down, each breath out a little longer than the one in
Lie down, stretch, and let your back sink into the bed
